verdict.line: You lose extended trades where Irelia lands E's stun and snowballs Ionian Fervor stacks, but you win the game once Blade Waltz comes online and your build outscales her, matching the 52.7% edge over 412 games.

brief.thesis: Irelia's lane pressure comes entirely from landing E (Flawless Duet) to stun and Mark you, which refreshes her Q (Bladesurge) and stacks Ionian Fervor for free attack speed and bonus damage — that's why she holds the lane advantage despite an even solo-kill rate. Fiora doesn't out-trade that combo pre-6; she out-scales it, turning the same skirmishes into kills once Blade Waltz and a Duelist-stacked build come online.

theirWindow.when: Her E lands its stun on you
theirWindow.what: She gets free stacked autos plus a Q reset off the Mark — expect a full follow-up combo. Flawless Duet is down for 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s afterward, so that's also your cue for when she can't threaten it again.

yourWindow.when: Her Q or E whiffs and she's committed
yourWindow.what: Riposte (W) up next basic attack for free damage, then Lunge (Q) in — you get the second dash within a couple seconds at no mana cost, so chase the reset instead of walking away.

powerCurve.note: E stun unlocks her Fervor snowball
Blade Waltz matches her Vanguard's Edge threat
Death's Dance sustain wins every skirmish

start.why: The 51.7% winrate pick (95.7% of games) — the lifesteal offsets her Q sustain and stacked-auto poke while you look for Lunge resets on minions.

boots.why: 56% winrate over 402 games — flat reduction on her Fervor-boosted autos and Q strikes is what actually swings extended trades, since her damage is almost entirely basic-attack based.

core.why: Cleave sustain plus burst lets you win all-ins even after she lands her stun, and the damage helps force Lunge resets in skirmishes.
Spellblade proc plus the move speed stacks with Burst of Speed (E) to actually catch her instead of watching her walk away post-stun.
Bleeds her stacked Fervor damage over time instead of eating it burst, which is what lets you survive her all-in window and win the counter-engage.

situational.when: you're ahead early and want to burst her down before she stacks Fervor rather than out-sustain her
the lane settles even and you'd rather split-push and force her to answer than keep trading

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the sustained-attack trade pattern Fiora wants (three hits) and the amp punishes her for standing still to charge Defiant Dance or land a stun.

summoners.why: The 52.8% winrate pick at 92.6% adoption — Ignite denies the heal off her Bladesurge and closes out the all-in before her stun timer resets, Flash extends your Lunge chase or gets you out of her E's stun range.

playing.title: Track Fervor stacks before committing
playing.detail: If she's already at multiple stacks from minion Q resets, she wins the extended trade even without landing E — back off and wait for her stacks to decay.

playing.title: Respect E's stun range at 850
playing.detail: Flawless Duet only hits what's caught between the two converging blades — stand on the far side of a minion wave so you're never in that line.

playing.title: Hold W for her post-engage auto
playing.detail: After she dashes in with Q or lands E, she immediately autos to cash in Fervor — that's the basic attack Riposte is built to parry and reflect.

playing.title: Chase resets with Lunge's second dash
playing.detail: Lunge can be performed a second time within a couple seconds at no mana cost — use it to close distance the instant she tries to walk away after whiffing.

playing.title: All-in at 6 on cooldown reads
playing.detail: Once Blade Waltz is up, look to engage right after she uses Q or E for wave clear — she has nothing left to punish your dash-in.

playing.title: Buy Hydra first for the sustain fight
playing.detail: You're not winning a pure poke war pre-6, so prioritize the item that lets you win the skirmish she starts, not avoid it.

playing.title: Duel confidently once Death's Dance is up
playing.detail: With Duelist stacking and DD's damage-over-time conversion online, side-lane 1v1s past level 13 favor you even if she's ahead on stacks.

brief.patchCaveat: Winrates, build order, boots, and runes here are pulled directly from measured Fiora vs Irelia games on the current patch via OP.GG; the trade timing, cooldown punishes, and stack-tracking advice are my own reading of the kits.

stats.opponentTip: Keep an eye out on Irelia’s (P) stacks when fighting her. It is ideal to block her (E) or (R) with [W].
